Cross-validated Verweij and van Houwelingen loss at a fixed coefficient vector

vvh_loss_fixed.Rd

Computes the cross-validated Verweij and van Houwelingen (V&VH) partial-likelihood loss for a coefficient vector that is held fixed across folds rather than refitted within each one.

The V&VH quantity is the difference between the log partial likelihood on the whole cohort and the log partial likelihood on the fold-complement, summed over folds and scaled by \(-2/n\). When a model is refitted inside each fold, that is what cv.coxkl and its siblings report. When the coefficient vector does not depend on the data at all – a published external model used unchanged – the same quantity is still well defined: the leave-fold-out coefficient simply equals the published vector on every fold.

This makes an externally published model directly comparable, on one common scale, with the fitted candidates. Supply the folds returned by the cv.* function so that every candidate is scored on the identical partition; scoring on a different split would make the comparison meaningless.

Usage

vvh_loss_fixed(
  z,
  delta,
  time,
  stratum = NULL,
  beta,
  folds,
  folds_sorted = TRUE,
  ties = c("none", "breslow")
)

Arguments

z

Numeric matrix or data frame of covariates, one row per subject.

delta

Event indicator, 1 for an event and 0 for right censoring.

time

Follow-up time.

stratum

Optional stratum labels. If NULL the whole cohort is treated as one stratum, matching cv.coxkl.

beta

The fixed coefficient vector. A named beta covering only a subset of colnames(z) is aligned by name and zero-padded, exactly as in align_beta; an unnamed one must have length ncol(z).

folds

Integer fold assignment, one entry per subject, as returned in the folds component of the cv.* functions.

folds_sorted

Whether folds is already expressed in the internally sorted row order. The cv.* functions return it that way, so the default is TRUE. Pass FALSE if folds follows the row order of z as supplied.

ties

Tie handling in the partial likelihood. "none" (the default, and the behaviour of every release before 1.3.0) takes subjects who share an event time in the order the sorted data list them, so each is dropped from the risk sets of the tied rows after it; "breslow" uses Breslow's approximation, in which the risk set at an event time is everyone whose time is that time or later. The two coincide when no event time is tied. The V&VH loss is computed on the chosen likelihood.

Value

A list with components

VVH_Loss

the cross-validated loss, on the same scale as the VVH_Loss column of cv.coxkl.

criteria

always "V&VH".

n

number of subjects.

nfolds

number of folds observed in folds.

per_fold

the per-fold contributions, before summation and scaling.

Details

The arithmetic reproduces cv.coxkl's "V&VH" branch exactly, including the summation over folds (a sum, not an average) and the \(-2/n\) scaling, so the number returned here is on the same scale as that function's VVH_Loss column and the two may be placed in one table.

No model is fitted. The routine evaluates one linear predictor and one partial likelihood per fold, so it is far cheaper than any of the cv.* functions.

See also

cv.coxkl, align_beta

Examples

data(ExampleData_lowdim)
tr <- ExampleData_lowdim$train
z  <- as.matrix(tr$z)
storage.mode(z) <- "double"

fit <- cv.coxkl(z = z, delta = tr$status, time = tr$time,
                beta = ExampleData_lowdim$beta_external_good,
                etas = c(0, 0.5, 2), nfolds = 5, seed = 1)
#> Warning: Stratum not provided. Treating all data as one stratum.

# the published model used unchanged, scored on the very same folds
ext <- vvh_loss_fixed(z = z, delta = tr$status, time = tr$time,
                      beta = ExampleData_lowdim$beta_external_good,
                      folds = fit$folds)
#> Warning: Stratum not provided. Treating all data as one stratum.
ext$VVH_Loss
#> [1] 2.443742
fit$internal_stat
#>   eta VVH_Loss
#> 1 0.0 2.600732
#> 2 0.5 2.502168
#> 3 2.0 2.454521
